title: SK Hynix converts ADR proceeds into booked EUV orders by Q2 2027
body: SK Hynix's $26.5 billion Nasdaq ADR sale — the largest US listing ever by a foreign company, seven times oversubscribed and up 14% on debut — is explicitly earmarked for expanding the Korean manufacturing base and buying equipment including EUV lithography scanners. That framing turns the listing from a financing event into a capacity commitment: HBM output is sold out against AI accelerator demand, EUV scanner slots at ASML are the binding constraint on any expansion, and a company holding fresh dollar-denominated capital has every incentive to lock delivery slots before competitors do. The prediction is that SK Hynix moves from earmark to contract quickly: within three quarters it discloses binding EUV scanner purchase commitments and a concrete Korean fab expansion schedule tied to the ADR proceeds, visible in its filings, earnings materials, or ASML's own bookings commentary. The scale of the raise makes silence unlikely — US investors who bought a seven-times-covered book on the HBM supply story will demand a deployment timeline, and the fastest credible proof is scanner orders on the books.

summary: SK Hynix's $26.5B ADR raise is earmarked for Korean fab expansion and EUV scanners. With HBM sold out and scanner slots the binding constraint, the capital should convert fast: expect disclosed EUV purchase commitments and a concrete capacity schedule in company filings by Q2 2027.
